item.title: DoorDash to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in USD 17 billion deal
item.description: US-based food delivery company DoorDash on Thursday announced an agreement to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in a deal valued at approximately USD 17 billion, as consolidation gathers ...
item.content:encoded:
DoorDash to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in USD 17 billion deal US-based food delivery company DoorDash on Thursday announced an agreement to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in a deal valued at approximately USD 17 billion, as consolidation gathers pace in the global food and grocery delivery market. ANI | Updated: 29-10-2026 21:38 IST | Created: 29-10-2026 21:38 IST

DoorDash logo (Photo/X@DoorDash). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US-based food delivery company DoorDash on Thursday announced an agreement to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in a deal valued at approximately USD 17 billion, as consolidation gathers pace in the global food and grocery delivery market. According to a joint statement issued by the two companies, DoorDash will acquire Instacart for USD 65 per share, representing a 26 per cent premium to Instacart's closing share price on October 22, the last trading day before reports of a possible transaction emerged. "DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ: DASH) and Maplebear Inc. (d.b.a. Instacart, NASDAQ: CART) today announced a definitive agreement under which DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a total value of $65.00 for each Instacart share, or an equity value of approximately $17 billion," the companies said in the statement. The transaction will involve at least 75 per cent cash, while DoorDash shares will account for no more than 25 per cent of the total consideration. Instacart shareholders can choose to receive cash, DoorDash shares or a combination of both, subject to certain conditions. Shares of DoorDash rose nearly 6 per cent in early US trading on Thursday, following the acquisition announcement and stronger-than-expected quarterly revenue. Instacart shares were largely unchanged at USD 58.35, according to Reuters. The acquisition comes amid growing consolidation in the global food delivery industry, as companies face rising operating costs, increasing competition and pressure to expand beyond restaurant deliveries. The industry has witnessed several major transactions, including DoorDash's acquisition of Deliveroo in 2025 and Uber's agreement to acquire Germany's Delivery Hero in July 2026. The proposed acquisition will combine DoorDash's delivery network with Instacart's grocery technology and retail partnerships, strengthening its position against large retailers such as Amazon and Walmart. Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, said, "Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day." The companies said Instacart customers could gain access to more than 50,000 additional stores. They also plan to combine DashPass and Instacart+ memberships, potentially saving subscribers an estimated USD 100 million annually. Following the acquisition, DoorDash expects to retain Instacart's brand, application and enterprise technology products. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, subject to Instacart shareholder approval and regulatory clearances, including antitrust review in the United States. Until then, both companies will continue operating independently. (ANI)

item.title: US weekly unemployment claims fall to 194,000, hover near 57-year lows
item.description: The number of Americans filing new applications for unemployment benefits declined by 1,000 to 194,000 in the week ending October 24, 2026, while continuing jobless claims fell by 21,000 to 1.701 ...
item.content:encoded:
US weekly unemployment claims fall to 194,000, hover near 57-year lows The number of Americans filing new applications for unemployment benefits declined by 1,000 to 194,000 in the week ending October 24, 2026, while continuing jobless claims fell by 21,000 to 1.701 million. ANI | Updated: 29-10-2026 19:42 IST | Created: 29-10-2026 19:42 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The number of Americans filing new applications for unemployment benefits declined by 1,000 to 194,000 in the week ending October 24, 2026, while continuing jobless claims fell by 21,000 to 1.701 million, according to data released by the US Department of Labor on Thursday. The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits hovered near 57-year lows last week amid labour market resilience. Claims are within striking distance of the 189,000 level touched in mid-July, which was the lowest reading since 1969. The department's Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims report showed that seasonally adjusted initial jobless claims decreased from the previous week's revised level of 195,000. "In the week ending October 24, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial claims was 194,000, a decrease of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level," the release stated. The previous week's initial claims figure was revised upward by 1,000, from 194,000 to 195,000. The four-week moving average of initial claims, which helps smooth weekly fluctuations, declined by 1,250 to 196,750 from the previous week's revised average of 198,000. The report also showed a decline in the number of Americans continuing to receive unemployment benefits. Seasonally adjusted insured unemployment stood at 1,701,000 in the week ending October 17, down by 21,000 from the previous week's revised level of 1,722,000. The previous week's continuing claims figure was revised downward by 6,000, from 1,728,000 to 1,722,000. However, the four-week moving average of insured unemployment increased marginally by 500 to 1,710,000. The seasonally adjusted insured unemployment rate remained unchanged at 1.1 per cent during the week ending October 17. On an unadjusted basis, actual initial claims under state unemployment programmes increased by 5,648, or 3.3 per cent, to 178,851 in the week ending October 24. Seasonal factors had projected an increase of 6,040 claims, or 3.5 per cent, during the week. In the corresponding week of 2025, unadjusted initial claims stood at 203,012. The advance unadjusted insured unemployment rate remained unchanged at 1 per cent during the week ending October 17. Meanwhile, unadjusted insured unemployment increased by 14,007, or 0.9 per cent, to 1,490,071, compared with 1,708,691 in the corresponding period last year. The report further showed that total continued weeks claimed for benefits across all unemployment insurance programmes reached 1,500,078 in the week ending October 10, an increase of 14,467 from the preceding week. The corresponding figure stood at 1,712,123 a year earlier. State-wise data showed that Michigan recorded the largest increase in initial claims for the week ending October 17, with an additional 1,906 applications, followed by Kentucky at 471 and South Carolina at 419. Conversely, Ohio registered the largest decline of 4,478 claims, followed by Tennessee with 2,635 fewer claims and California with a decrease of 1,930. The department also reported that no state was triggered onto the Extended Benefits programme during the week ending October 10. (ANI)

item.description: The US economy grew at an annualised rate of 3.4 per cent in the July–September quarter of 2026, accelerating from 2.2 per cent in the previous quarter and exceeding market expectations, according to ...
item.content:encoded:
US GDP growth accelerates to 3.4 pc in Q3 2026, up from 2.2 pc in previous quarter The US economy grew at an annualised rate of 3.4 per cent in the July–September quarter of 2026, accelerating from 2.2 per cent in the previous quarter and exceeding market expectations, according to an advance estimate released by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on Thursday. ANI | Updated: 29-10-2026 18:45 IST | Created: 29-10-2026 18:45 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The US economy grew at an annualised rate of 3.4 per cent in the July–September quarter of 2026, accelerating from 2.2 per cent in the previous quarter and exceeding market expectations, according to an advance estimate released by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on Thursday. “Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 3.4 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the advance estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis,” the release stated. The BEA said investment, consumer spending and government expenditure contributed to the expansion. However, lower exports and higher imports partly offset the increase. “The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased,” it said. The economy grew faster during the quarter mainly because of an acceleration in investment and a return to growth in government spending. These gains were partly offset by a decline in exports, while imports increased at a faster rate than in the previous quarter. Investment growth was led by private inventories and equipment. Within equipment, information-processing equipment - mainly computers and peripheral equipment - made the largest contribution. Consumer spending increased across both services and goods. The rise in services was led by healthcare, food services and accommodation, while spending on goods was supported mainly by prescription drugs. A measure of underlying private domestic demand also remained strong. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers—which includes consumer spending and private fixed investment - increased 4.9 per cent in the third quarter, compared with 4.6 per cent in the previous three months. Price pressures measured within the GDP report moderated during the quarter. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 3 per cent, compared with 5.6 per cent in the second quarter. The personal consumption expenditure price index increased at an annualised rate of 2.1 per cent during the quarter, slowing from 5 per cent in the previous quarter. Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index rose 2.5 per cent, compared with 3.3 per cent in the second quarter. (ANI)

item.title: Israel President Herzog calls for probe into claims of foreign influence in elections, cautions against targeting Arab voters
item.description: These remarks came after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his political allies accused opponents of electoral bribery intended to drive up Arab voting numbers.
item.content:encoded:
Israel President Herzog calls for probe into claims of foreign influence in elections, cautions against targeting Arab voters These remarks came after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his political allies accused opponents of electoral bribery intended to drive up Arab voting numbers. ANI | Updated: 29-10-2026 17:53 IST | Created: 29-10-2026 17:53 IST

Israeli President Isaac Herzog (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Israeli President Isaac Herzog has stated that he held discussions with Central Elections Committee chief Noam Sohlberg and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) chief David Zini following Sohlberg’s request to probe allegations of external interference in Tuesday's election. According to the Times of Israel, Herzog, speaking from the President’s Residence, emphasised the necessity of a rigorous review while warning against unfairly maligning the broader Arab populace. “I am closely following developments in the investigation into the suspicions reported this morning. The integrity of elections is a paramount value in a democracy. The evidence and suspicions must be thoroughly investigated, and the offenders must be investigated and punished to the fullest extent of the law,” he stated. These remarks came after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his political allies accused opponents of electoral bribery intended to drive up Arab voting numbers. Herzog cautioned, "But even at a moment like this, we must avoid tarnishing an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote and take an active part in democracy.” The Times of Israel further noted that Herzog renewed his plea to political leaders to enter upcoming government negotiations with an “open” mind and prioritise solely “what is in the best interests of the country”. Subsequently, the Times of Israel, citing Hebrew media outlets, reported that Shin Bet chief David Zini met yesterday with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to deliberate on the foreign election interference probe. According to those reports, the meeting was requested by the Shin Bet, which had already initiated its investigation into the matter prior to election day. Additionally, Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot met with Zini this morning, the Times of Israel reported, as per the party statement. “During the meeting, he was updated on the suspicions regarding foreign interference in the election in Israel. Eisenkot offered his support for the Shin Bet and law enforcement officials for a swift and transparent investigation,” the party stated. This comes as the Shin Bet probes allegations of possible foreign interference in the recently concluded Knesset elections after the decision of the Israel Election Committee to order an investigation into allegations, which has created a political firestorm in Jerusalem. The call to action follows Israeli Central Elections Committee Chair Justice Noam Sohlberg asking Shin Bet chief David Zini to investigate allegations of foreign interference in Tuesday’s election. Shin Bet is currently probing allegations of Qatari influence in the recently concluded elections. (ANI)
